schema.title: Response List Memories Api Memories Get V1

get.description: Memories predicted to be nearly forgotten — the review queue.

schema.title: Response List Fading Memories Api Memories Fading Get V1

get.description:
Spaced-repetition review queue — fading, unpinned, un-snoozed memories
due for a keep/reinforce/weaken/pin/forget/snooze decision.

Candidates the admission gate answered ``review`` for and parked for a
human — near-duplicates it declined to decide on its own.

Distinct from ``/api/memories/review``, which is the spaced-repetition queue
over memories that were already admitted. Nothing listed here is a memory
yet. ``status=""`` returns every decision state, which is how the queue
doubles as a record of what was decided.

post.description:
Keep a held candidate: store it as the memory it was going to be, with
the importance, tags, session, project, source and type it arrived with.

Drop a held candidate. The row stays with its verdict, so a discard is
recorded rather than leaving no trace.

get.description:
Read-only scan for secrets (credentials, tokens) that slipped into
stored memories before the admission gate existed.

post.description:
Bulk redaction of secrets across stored memories. dry_run=true
(default) only previews; set false to rewrite every flagged memory.

get.description:
Stored memories whose provenance/trust confidence is below
``threshold`` (least confident first). Run trust/recompute first to
populate. Provenance is NOT truth — it does not change H-score ranking.

post.description: Compute and persist the provenance/trust score for every memory.

Ask your memory a question and get a synthesized, cited answer.

Grounded only in stored memories; each source is returned so the UI can
show citations. Read-only — asking does not reinforce memories. Uses an LLM
when OPENAI_API_KEY is set, otherwise returns ranked evidence (offline).
Find (dry_run) or remove near-duplicate memories.

Preview (dry_run) or apply sleep-like consolidation: cluster related
older memories and compress each cluster into one consolidated memory,
archiving the originals inside it.

Preview the admission gate's verdict for a candidate memory WITHOUT
storing it: admit / review / redact / reject.

Store a candidate memory through the admission gate: dedupe + secret
redaction. reject/review are not stored unless force=True.
Store an uploaded file locally and return the path to attach from.

Attach a local file to a memory by reference (path + sha256), with
optional derived text (OCR/transcript/caption) that recall actually
searches over.

Re-check the file against what was recorded at attach time. A missing
or changed file raises a conflict candidate rather than silently altering
the memory — see /api/conflicts.
Apply a spaced-repetition review decision to a memory.

Manually strengthen a memory — resets its decay clock and grows its
stability, the same reinforcement that happens automatically on recall.

Learn from recall outcomes: helpful=true reinforces the memory,
helpful=false weakens it so wrong/stale information fades out fast.

Strip secrets from an already-stored memory in place, recorded
auditably in its metadata's redaction_history.

Hard-delete a memory across every layer and verify nothing survives.
Pinned memories are purged too — this is a deliberate human action.

get.description:
Predicted retention curve for a memory — powers the 'memory strength'
visualization in the dashboard's detail drawer.

Provenance/trust breakdown for a memory — explainable, deterministic,
NOT truth, and independent of H-score recall ranking.

Memories most similar to this one — the 'related memories' graph edge,
computed live from embeddings. Powers 'see also' in the detail drawer.

Return H(x,ψ) score breakdown for a specific memory + query pair.

If query is empty, memory.content is used as the default query so the
breakdown reflects self-similarity (baseline score for the memory).

Delegates to ``engine.score_breakdown`` — the single source of truth for
cosine/decay/scoring math — and reshapes its result into the public API
schema. Contract: 404 unknown memory, 400 memory without embedding or
with a mismatched embedding dimension.

schema.title: Response List Sessions Api Sessions Get V1

delete.description:
Delete a session, saying what happens to its memories.

``memories=refuse`` (default) deletes only an empty session and answers 409
with the count otherwise — tidying up a session must not quietly take
memories with it. ``detach`` keeps the memories and drops their session
link; ``delete`` removes them too, through the same cascade a single
memory delete uses.

post.description:
Distill a session's memories into one durable summary memory (LLM when
OPENAI_API_KEY is set, deterministic extractive fallback otherwise).
Record an agent connecting to LEVH.
Send a heartbeat to keep an agent connection alive.
Disconnect an agent from LEVH.

get.description: List all agent connections (active and disconnected).

get.description: Real first-run readiness derived from local storage/configuration.

post.description: Generate a focused MCP client config without persisting secrets.
Remove only metadata.demo=true memories using the audited purge path.

get.description:
Distinct people across all memories (calendar attendees, email
senders/recipients, transcript speakers), most-frequent first.

A person's profile plus every memory that mentions them. ``key`` may be
an email, a person key, or a free-text name (resolved by best match).

Episodic memories grouped by day, most recent first — "what happened
this/last week".

Deterministic Daily Briefing — what's on today, open commitments from
recent memories, and memories that are fading and may need review.

Proactive pre-meeting brief — the next upcoming meeting (or a matched
one), each attendee's recent context, and relevant open commitments and
decisions. Deterministic, offline.

Distinct organizations across all memories (people grouped by email
domain), most-frequent first.

An organization's profile plus every memory that mentions someone from
it. ``key`` may be a domain or a free-text name (resolved by best match).

Deterministic decision detection — statements like "we decided" /
"agreed to" / "karar verdik" in recent episodic memory content.

post.description: Generate a CLAUDE.md / .cursorrules style context file from memories.

get.description: Current server configuration (for the Settings page).

Prometheus text exposition of this process's counters (issue #145).

Scrapeable at ``/api/metrics`` and its versioned alias ``/api/v1/metrics``.
The engine, the routes and the counters share one process, so the registry
is process-wide and this handler is a read with no engine dependency —
answering must not itself touch the database it reports on.

Readiness probe: this process can actually serve reads and writes.

``/api/health`` is liveness — it answers from the process's own state and
stays up even when the database is locked or the embedder is broken. That
made the Docker ``HEALTHCHECK`` a lie: a wedged server still reported
healthy (issue #145). This endpoint does the work liveness must not: it
pings SQLite, reports the embedder mode actually running and whether a
derived-state rebuild is behind.

Failure is a 503 with the reasons, so an orchestrator that reads the status
code (not the body) still routes around a broken instance. The body is the
same shape either way.

post.description:
Run the recall-quality benchmark harness (hit@k / MRR on a labelled
corpus) and return the metrics — powers the Settings 'Recall Quality'
panel. Runs against an isolated temp DB/engine, never touches real data.

get.description:
One-shot audit bundle: memories, entity graph, trust scores, and
conflict candidates — the raw machine-readable record.
Raw SQLite copy of the live database, taken via the online backup API.

Human-readable audit report (summary counts, entity/trust/conflict
overview) rendered from the same data as the JSON export.

post.description:
Full portable snapshot (all memories + sessions) as a downloadable
file. When ``passphrase`` is set the file is encrypted at rest
(AES-128 via Fernet, PBKDF2-derived key); otherwise it's plain JSON.
Returns the raw bytes with a suggested filename.

Restore from a backup file. ``content_b64`` is the base64-encoded
backup bytes (encrypted or plain — auto-detected). ``passphrase`` is
required only for encrypted files. ``replace=true`` first creates a local
SQLite safety backup, then replaces the current store; the default merges.

Turn an arbitrary uploaded file into memories.

Plain text, PDF, Word, Excel and zip archives are extracted to text and
admitted as one or more memories (split on paragraph boundaries for long
content). Formats with no extractor still get a memory recording that
the file arrived, so nothing silently disappears. Same base64-in-JSON
shape as ``/api/restore`` and ``/api/connectors/upload`` — keeps
python-multipart out of the runtime dependency list.
Import data from an external app via connector.

Connector v2 ingest: fetch, then route items through the admission
gate (dedupe + secret redaction), with incremental sync bookkeeping.
Store an uploaded file locally and return the path to import from.

get.description: List available connectors and their status.
Get required config fields for a connector.

post.description: Rebuild the persistent entity graph from every stored memory.

get.description: Counts of persisted entities by type.
Persisted entities (optionally filtered by type), most-mentioned first.

An entity's profile: the memories that mention it and the entities it
co-occurs with. ``entity_id`` may be a full id like ``person:alice@acme.com``
or a free-text query (resolved by best match).
List recorded mistakes, newest first. ``days=0`` means all time.
List the pinned rules mistakes have produced, most important first.

post.description:
Judge a proposed action against the recorded rules, before it runs.

Read-only and advisory: returns ``warn`` when a recorded rule overlaps the
action and ``allow`` otherwise. It never returns ``block`` — the caller
decides whether a warning is an instruction.
Record a mistake as a pinned rule plus a violation row.

Scan stored memories for conflict CANDIDATES — pairs that share an
entity and show an opposing surface pattern. Idempotent: never resets
already-reviewed candidates.

get.description:
List conflict candidates, optionally filtered by status. Pass an empty
status to list every status.

post.description:
Apply a human review decision to a conflict candidate. ``conflict_id``
may contain ``|`` so the path converter is used.

get.description:
List findings, newest sighting first. Pass an empty status for all
states — that is the "what did we decide about these" view.

post.description:
Record a finding. Scrubbed and fingerprinted before it is stored, so a
repeat folds into the existing row instead of creating a new one.
Apply a human decision: ack, resolved or ignored (open reopens it).

get.description:
Tarama sonucu; hiçbir şey yazmaz.

``scan`` senkron: dosya sistemini gezip SQLite sorguluyor. Doğrudan
çağrılsaydı bu rota, işi sürerken sunucunun TÜM isteklerini bekletirdi —
tek bir event loop var ve senkron kod onu bırakmaz.

workspace_id.title: Workspace Id
workspace_id.description: The tenancy boundary this memory belongs to (issue #302). A single-user install has exactly one, ``default``; the field exists so a future shared/team server scopes storage by workspace rather than bolting identity on afterwards. ``project`` stays a recall label *inside* a workspace, not a security boundary.

stability_hours.title: Stability Hours
stability_hours.description: This memory's own half-life in hours — how long until it decays to 50% relevance since last access. Grows every time the memory is recalled or explicitly reinforced (spaced-repetition style), so frequently-used memories become durable while unused ones fade.

recall_count.title: Recall Count
recall_count.description: Times this memory has been reinforced by recall.

valid_from.title: Valid From
valid_from.description: World time from which this fact was believed true (issue #335). Defaults to created_at at write; NULL only for a row that predates the column and has not been backfilled.

valid_to.title: Valid To
valid_to.description: World time at which this fact stopped being current. NULL means 'still believed'. Set when a newer, near-identical memory supersedes this one. A retired row is never deleted and is reachable through an as_of read.

superseded_by.title: Superseded By
superseded_by.description: Id of the memory that replaced this one, if any (issue #335).

workspace_id.description: The tenancy boundary this memory belongs to (issue #302). A single-user install has exactly one, ``default``; the field exists so a future shared/team server scopes storage by workspace rather than bolting identity on afterwards. ``project`` stays a recall label *inside* a workspace, not a security boundary.

stability_hours.description: This memory's own half-life in hours — how long until it decays to 50% relevance since last access. Grows every time the memory is recalled or explicitly reinforced (spaced-repetition style), so frequently-used memories become durable while unused ones fade.

MemoryOut.title: MemoryOut
MemoryOut.description:
A memory as the HTTP surface returns it: embedding dropped (large and
useless to a client - similarity is computed server-side) and attachments
joined where the route does that.

MemoryStats.title: MemoryStats
MemoryStats.description: Aggregate statistics about the memory system.

NameCountOut.title: NameCountOut
NameCountOut.description: Shared row shape of the project/source/tag aggregates.

OrganizationOut.title: OrganizationOut
OrganizationOut.description: An aggregated organization (people capped at 50 in the summary).

PersonOut.title: PersonOut
PersonOut.description: An aggregated person (``memory_ids`` dropped for the summary view).

explain.title: Explain
explain.description: Return a per-result score breakdown: which signal drove the ranking, where each candidate came from, and the four H(x,ψ) penalties that sum to the score. Off by default; the ranking is identical either way.

reinforce.title: Reinforce
reinforce.description: Whether this recall reinforces the returned memories (resets decay clock, bumps frequency). Set false for read-only dashboard/search previews so browsing doesn't inflate the signal.

as_of.title: As Of
as_of.description: Point-in-time read (issue #335): return what the store believed on this ISO-8601 instant, including facts retired since. Always read-only — a question about the past never reinforces a current belief.

include_superseded.title: Include Superseded
include_superseded.description: Opt retired facts back into the candidate set (issue #335). Off by default: a superseded fact is not current and must not surface in an ordinary read. Set true to audit what was replaced.

ReviewMemoryResponse.title: ReviewMemoryResponse
ReviewMemoryResponse.description: The result of a spaced-repetition review decision.

ServerConfigResponse.title: ServerConfigResponse
ServerConfigResponse.description:
``GET /api/config`` — the Settings page payload. Free-form in shape by

Session.title: Session

SessionDeleteResponse.description:
``DELETE /api/sessions/{id}`` - what happened to the session and its

StoreDecision.title: StoreDecision
StoreDecision.description: The admission gate's verdict over one write (from ``admission.evaluate``).
